---
title: "SPEC-v0.4.0"
subtitle: "yrAiProject: new, status, update; the parts of a project; pending work; the setup notice; version 0.4.0"
---

## Purpose {#sec-purpose}

Every project for AI-assisted work has the same base:

- rules that every AI agent and every collaborator reads;
- a list of pending work (things to do later), kept as GitHub issues;
- for new projects, and for existing ones that want it, a Quarto book of project documents (SPECs, guides,
  plans), with a skill to add documents. Work to do later is not a document: it is pending items;
- a clear notice, for people and for AI agents, that `yrAiProject.sh` set up the project, which files it installed,
  and who changes each one (@sec-notice).

One command, `yrAiProject.sh`, makes new projects, reports the state of any project, and sets up or updates
existing projects. Before it changes a project, it shows what it would change and asks. The user guide
(`USER-GUIDE-v001.qmd`) tells how to use it. This SPEC says what it must do.

## Changes from SPEC-v0.3.0 {#sec-changes}

- **The setup notice** (@sec-notice). Each project shows that `yrAiProject.sh` set it up, in five places:
  - `.yrAiProject/README.md`: for people and agents, the version, the parts, each installed file and who changes
    it, how to change things, the commands, and the history;
  - a SessionStart hook of the `rules` part, which shows a one-line notice at the start of each Claude Code session
    (from `.yrAiProject/session-start.json`);
  - the block "yrAiProject setup" near the top of `AGENTS.md`, which every AI agent reads;
  - the block "yrAiProject setup" at the end of `README.md`, if the project has a README;
  - in the docs book: a notice on the home page, and the chapter `docs/PROJECT-SETUP.qmd`, which shows
    `.yrAiProject/README.md`.
- **The record** gets a history: one entry for each `new` and `update` that writes it (@sec-manifest).
- **The first commit** of `new` says what the tool made, and names `.yrAiProject/README.md`.
- **`status`** reports a setup notice that is missing or out of date.
- **Template v0.4.0:**
  - the `.claude/settings.json` has the notice hook before the pending-work hook;
  - `AGENTS.md` and the READMEs have the empty setup blocks; the `AGENTS.md` line about the template version moves
    into the block;
  - the docs book has `PROJECT-SETUP.qmd` after `index.qmd`, and the home page has the notice;
  - the DOC-GUIDE names the two pages that have no version;
  - the `.gitignore` files have the line `**/*.quarto_ipynb`. Quarto 1.5 and later add that line to a book
    folder's `.gitignore` at the first render if it is missing; then the project had an uncommitted change.

  Template v0.3.0 does not change.

The changes from SPEC-v0.2.0 to SPEC-v0.3.0 are in SPEC-v0.3.0.

## Repository layout {#sec-layout}

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `templates/vX.Y.Z/shared/` | Files for every project of that version |
| `templates/vX.Y.Z/TYPE/` | Files for one type of new project (`work`, `book`) |
| `rules/AGENTS.md` | The shared rules: the text from its first `## ` heading on |
| `bin/yrAiProject.py` | The tool (Python 3.8 or later, standard library only) |
| `tests/selftest.py` | The tests |
| `docs/` | This book |

The command `yrAiProject.sh` is a wrapper in the Dropbox tools folder. It finds the repository by a path relative
to its own folder (`../_yrAiCoding/yrAiProjectTemplates`), and runs the Python script with the first of `python3`,
`python` and `py -3` that runs Python 3.8 or later.

## Template versions {#sec-versions}

1. A version folder name is `v` and three numbers. The newest version (highest numbers) is the default.
2. A version is released when the repository has the git tag `templates-vX.Y.Z`. The files of a released
   version must not change. A change goes into a new version folder, which has its own SPEC.
3. The type folders of a version are its types. The `shared` folder is not a type.

## The parts of a project {#sec-parts}

| Part | Files | New project | `update` of an existing folder |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | `AGENTS.md` (the setup block and the shared-rules block), `CLAUDE.md` (the line `@AGENTS.md`), the notice hook in `.claude/settings.json`, the setup block in `README.md`, `.yrAiProject/` | yes | always |
| `pending-work` | `.claude/skills/pending-work/**`, the SessionStart hook in `.claude/settings.json` | yes | yes, unless `--no-pending-work` |
| `docs` | `docs/**` (with `PROJECT-SETUP.qmd`), `.claude/skills/new-doc/**` | yes | only with `--with-docs`, or if the project has it |
| (base) | `README.md`, `.gitignore`, and the files of the type (the main book of a `book` project) | yes | never |

1. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `README.md` and `docs/_quarto.yml` are **merged**: the tool
   changes only its blocks, its line or its hooks, and keeps the rest of the file (@sec-rules, @sec-notice,
   @sec-pending). `update` does not create a `README.md`.
2. The other files are of two kinds:
   - **tool files**: the files under `.claude/skills/`, the guides `docs/NAME-GUIDE-vNNN.qmd`, and
     `docs/PROJECT-SETUP.qmd`. `update` keeps
     them up to date, unless they were changed by hand (@sec-update);
   - **starting files**: all the others (the README, the first SPEC, `_quarto.yml`, ...). The
     project owns them: the tool adds each one once, and never changes it.
3. `update` uses the `shared/` files of the version only; the type folders are for `new`.

## Placeholders {#sec-placeholders}

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{{YRAI:KEY}}` | A value that the tool fills in. `KEY` is capital letters, digits and `_` |
| `<!-- YRAI:BEGIN:NAME -->` ... `<!-- YRAI:END:NAME -->` | A region that the user writes. The markers stay in the file |

The tool fills these values:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `PROJECT_NAME` | The folder name |
| `PROJECT_TITLE` | `--title`, the recorded title, or the folder name |
| `PROJECT_DESCRIPTION` | `--description`, the recorded description, or a TODO line |
| `PROJECT_TYPE` | The type (`work` for a folder set up by `update`) |
| `CREATED_DATE` | The recorded date, or today, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `TEMPLATE_VERSION` | The version, `vX.Y.Z` |

1. In `.yml` files, and in the YAML front matter of `.qmd` and `.md` files, a template puts each value in double
   quotes. The tool escapes `\` and `"` in those values.
2. A key that the tool does not know stays as it is.
3. Tool files have no placeholders, so their fingerprints do not depend on the values.

## The shared rules {#sec-rules}

1. The shared block is the text of `rules/AGENTS.md` from its first `## ` heading on, between the line
   `<!-- begin shared rules: copied by yrAiProject from yrAiProjectTemplates/rules/AGENTS.md; edit there -->` and
   the line `<!-- end shared rules -->`. (The environment variable `AGENTS_SHARED_RULES=FILE` gives another source.)
2. In a project's `AGENTS.md`, the tool replaces the text from a line that starts with `<!-- begin shared rules`
   to the line `<!-- end shared rules -->`, and keeps the rest of the file. If there is no block, it adds the block
   at the end. A begin line without an end line is an error (exit 2). If there is no `AGENTS.md`, `update` creates
   one with a title and the block.
3. `CLAUDE.md` gets the line `@AGENTS.md` at the top, or is created with that line. The tool does not write through
   a symlink.
4. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` on the owner's computers imports `rules/AGENTS.md` (`setup-computer`, @sec-tool-other).

## The setup notice {#sec-notice}

`new` and `update` write the notice each time that they write the record. Its text comes from the record only (the
version, the parts, the files, the history), so `status` can check it.

1. **`.yrAiProject/README.md`** has no `#` title (the docs page gives the title). It starts with the bold line
   "Project setup by yrAiProject.sh" and the link to this repository. Then:
   - a table: the template version, the parts, "set up by" (`new`, with the type, or `update`), and the date of the
     last change;
   - "The parts": one line for each installed part;
   - "The files": a table of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json` (if it exists), `README.md` (if it
     exists), each file of the record's `files`, and `.yrAiProject/`, with the part and who changes the file: you;
     you, and the tool only its block, line or hooks; or the tool (a tool file: `update` replaces it, unless it was
     changed by hand);
   - "How to change things", "Commands" (`status`, `update --dry-run`, `update`), and "History" (a table of the
     record's history).
2. **`.yrAiProject/session-start.json`** is the JSON output of a SessionStart hook:
   - `systemMessage`, for the user: `Set up by yrAiProject.sh (yrAiProjectTemplates VERSION; parts: PARTS). Before
     you change its files, read .yrAiProject/README.md.`;
   - `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, for the agent: the same facts, the files not to edit, and the
     commands.
3. **The hook** is the first SessionStart entry of `.claude/settings.json`, for the sources `startup` and `clear`:
   `cat "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.yrAiProject/session-start.json" 2>/dev/null || true`. It needs only `cat`, so it also
   runs in Git Bash on Windows. Without the file, it prints nothing and does not fail. Claude Code runs all the
   SessionStart hooks, and gives the agent the text of each one.
4. **The block in `AGENTS.md`** is between a line that starts with `<!-- begin yrAiProject setup` and the line
   `<!-- end yrAiProject setup -->`. It has the heading "Set up by yrAiProject.sh", the version and the parts, a
   pointer to `.yrAiProject/README.md`, the files not to edit, and an instruction for agents without the hook: tell
   the user in one line at the start of a session, unless a SessionStart message did. The tool replaces the block.
   If there is none, it puts the block after the `#` title line (or at the top of a file without one).
5. **The block in `README.md`** has the same markers, and one sentence in italics. If there is none, the tool adds
   it at the end. A begin line without an end line, in either file, is an error (exit 2).
6. **In the docs book:** `docs/PROJECT-SETUP.qmd` (title "Project setup by yrAiProject.sh") includes
   `../.yrAiProject/README.md`. `docs/_quarto.yml` lists it after `index.qmd`: in a project of an older version,
   `update` adds the line after the line `- index.qmd`, or, if there is no such line, says to add it by hand. The
   template's `docs/index.qmd` starts with a notice that links to the page; `update` does not change an existing
   `index.qmd`.

## The record {#sec-manifest}

`.yrAiProject/manifest.json`, schema 3:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "version": "v0.4.0",
  "projectType": "work",
  "parts": ["docs", "pending-work", "rules"],
  "skippedParts": [],
  "values": {"PROJECT_NAME": "...", "PROJECT_TITLE": "...", "PROJECT_DESCRIPTION": "...",
             "PROJECT_TYPE": "work", "CREATED_DATE": "2026-10-12", "TEMPLATE_VERSION": "v0.4.0"},
  "history": [{"date": "2026-10-12", "command": "new", "version": "v0.4.0", "parts": ["docs", "pending-work", "rules"]}],
  "files": {".claude/skills/pending-work/SKILL.md": "<SHA-256 of the text as installed>", "...": "..."},
  "createdAt": "2026-10-12T18:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-12T18:00:00Z",
  "tool": {"name": "yrAiProject", "version": "0.4.0", "templatesCommit": "abc1234"}
}
```

1. `projectType` is `null` for a folder that `update` set up.
2. `skippedParts` holds `pending-work` after `update --no-pending-work`, so that later updates do not add it.
3. `files` has a fingerprint for each file that the tool added or changed, and for each tool file that it found up
   to date. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text with `\n` line ends. The merged files have none.
4. `history` has one entry for each run of `new` and `update` that wrote the record. A record from before v0.4.0
   has no `history`: the first update starts it with an entry "set up (no history before v0.4.0)" on the date of
   `createdAt`.
5. The tool does not read the records of older tools (`.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json`); `status` notes one.

## yrAiProject {#sec-tool}

`yrAiProject.sh COMMAND [PATH] [OPTIONS]`. For `status` and `update`, `PATH` defaults to the top of the current git
repository, else the current folder. No command, `-h`, `--help` or `help`: the help, exit 0. An unknown command or
option: exit 2.

### Confirmation {#sec-confirm}

1. `new` and `update` first print the plan: each file that they would add (`+ add`) or change (`~ change`), the
   record, and each file that they leave alone with the reason (`= keep`). `update` also prints a unified diff of
   each file that it would change, and of each merged file that it would create.
2. Then they ask `Apply these changes? [y/N]`. Only `y` or `yes` applies. Any other answer: "Nothing was
   changed", exit 1.
3. `-y` (`--yes`) applies without the question. `--dry-run` prints the plan and "nothing was changed", exit 0.
4. If standard input is not a terminal and there is no `-y`, the tool prints the plan, changes nothing, and exits
   with status 6, with a message that names `-y` and `--dry-run`. It never waits for an answer that cannot come.

### new {#sec-tool-new}

1. `PATH` must not exist, or be empty, or hold only `.git`. With `--strict-empty`, `.git` alone is refused.
   Otherwise: exit 3, and the message names `update` and `status`.
2. `--type` (`work`, the default, or `book`), `--version` (the newest by default), `--title`, `--description`.
   An unknown type or version: exit 2.
3. With `--github`, the tool first checks that `gh` exists and is logged in (else exit 2).
4. The plan lists every file. After confirmation, the tool writes the `shared` files, then the type files (a type
   file replaces a shared file with the same path), with the values filled in and the file permissions kept. It
   skips `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.quarto`, `_book` and `.DS_Store`. It fills in the shared rules and the setup
   blocks, and writes the record with every part that the version has, and the setup notice (@sec-notice).
5. If the folder has no `.git`, it runs `git init -b main`. It commits all the files ("Make NAME from
   yrAiProjectTemplates VERSION (TYPE project)", with a second paragraph that names the parts and
   `.yrAiProject/README.md`). A git failure: exit 5.
6. With `--github`, it runs `gh repo create NAME --private --source PATH --remote origin --push`, then
   `pending.sh setup-labels` if the project has the pending-work part. A failure of `gh repo create`: exit 5, and
   the local project stays. A failure of `setup-labels` is a warning.

### status {#sec-status}

`status` changes nothing. It prints:

1. the state: "set up with yrAiProject, template VERSION (DATE)", with "the newest version is ..." if it is older;
   or "partly set up: it has PARTS, but no record of a version" (a project without a record that has the
   shared-rules block, the pending-work skill or hook, or the docs book with the new-doc skill); or "not set up
   with yrAiProject";
2. one line for each part: up to date; out of date (what `update` would add and change); not installed (and
   whether `update` adds it, or how to add it); and the number of files changed by hand, which `update` leaves
   alone;
3. "setup notice out of date or missing" if `.yrAiProject/README.md` or `session-start.json` is not what the
   record makes; else the path of `.yrAiProject/README.md`;
4. notes (for example a record of an older tool, or a `docs/_quarto.yml` that is not from yrAiProject).

Exit 0 if `update` has nothing to do, else 1.

### update {#sec-update}

1. `PATH` must be a folder (else exit 2). It may be a project that was never set up.
2. The parts: the parts that the record lists (or, without a record, that the folder has), plus `rules`, plus
   `pending-work` unless `--no-pending-work` or the record's `skippedParts` (`--with-pending-work` removes it from
   there), plus `docs` with `--with-docs`. `--no-pending-work` with `--with-pending-work`: exit 2.
3. If `docs` would be added, but `docs/_quarto.yml` exists and is not from yrAiProject, the docs part is not added
   (a note says so).
4. For each `shared` file of the version in those parts:
   - a **tool file** that is missing is added (also if it was deleted); one that is the same as the template is up
     to date; one whose fingerprint is the recorded one is replaced (`~ change`, "a newer version"); any other one
     was changed by hand, or was not installed by yrAiProject, and is left alone (`= keep`);
   - a **starting file** is added if it does not exist and the record does not list it. Otherwise it is not
     touched, and not reported. If the project has no `README.md`, `docs/index.qmd` is added without its include of
     `../README.md` (Quarto cannot render an include of a missing file).
5. The merged files: the shared rules (@sec-rules); the setup blocks (@sec-notice); the SessionStart entries of the
   template's `.claude/settings.json`: the notice hook (`rules`) first, unless an entry already names
   `session-start.json`, and the pending-work hook at the end, unless an entry already runs `pending.sh`. The other
   settings are kept. A settings file that is not JSON, or has hooks in another form, is left alone with a note; the
   rest of the update goes on. With the docs part, `docs/_quarto.yml` gets the line for `PROJECT-SETUP.qmd`.
6. Before it asks, the tool warns if the folder is not a git repository, and lists the files that it would change
   and that have uncommitted changes.
7. After confirmation, it writes the files, the record and the setup notice, and says that nothing was committed. It makes no
   commit. If it added the pending-work part, it names `pending.sh setup-labels`.
8. If nothing would change and the record is current, it prints "Nothing to do", exit 0.

### list, setup-computer {#sec-tool-other}

- `list`: the versions, newest first, with their types.
- `setup-computer [--check]`: checks that the Dropbox tools folder (`../../tools` from this repository, with
  `yrAiProject.sh`) is on `PATH`, and only reports it; and makes `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` import `rules/AGENTS.md`
  (the line `@~/...` under the home folder): it adds the line, or creates the file. Safe to repeat. With
  `--check`, it changes nothing and exits with status 1 if something is missing.

### Exit status {#sec-exit}

0 OK (done, nothing to do, or `--dry-run`); 1 `status` found something to do, or the answer was no; 2 bad
options, a missing template or a missing tool; 3 `new`: `PATH` is not empty; 5 git or gh failed; 6 confirmation
needed, but there is no terminal.

### The old command names {#sec-stubs}

`yrNewAiProject.sh` and `agents-init.sh` in the tools folder print the `yrAiProject.sh` command that replaces each
of their uses, and exit with status 2 (`--help`: status 0). They do nothing else.

## The new-doc skill {#sec-documents}

1. Document types are names in capital letters, digits and hyphens. The default is `SPEC`. There are no PRDs.
2. A SPEC file is `SPEC-vX.Y.Z.qmd`. The default version is the newest SPEC's version with the last number plus 1,
   or `0.1.0` if there is no SPEC. `--version` gives another one.
3. Another type's file is `TYPE-vNNN.qmd`, with the next copy number (`001` first).
4. The new file is a copy of the newest version of its type, with the new title. With `--blank`, or when there is
   no older version, it is the outline of the type.
5. The script lists the file in `docs/_quarto.yml`: above the newest older version of the type; else at the end of
   its part (`Specification` for SPEC, `Guides` for a name that ends in `GUIDE`, else `Work`, or `--part`); else in
   a new part at the end of `book: chapters:`.
6. A file that exists is never replaced.

## Pending work {#sec-pending}

Pending items are things to do later. The user talks to the agent; the agent does the GitHub work.

1. An item is a GitHub issue in the project's repository (the `origin` remote) with the label `pending-work`, one
   category label (by default `fix`, `improvement`, `decision` or `recheck`) and one priority label
   (`priority: high`, `priority: medium` or `priority: low`).
2. `scripts/pending.sh` needs only bash and `gh` (it uses the jq that is built into `gh`), so it also runs in Git
   Bash on Windows. Its commands:

   | Command | What it does |
   |---|---|
   | `session-start` | Prints the JSON for the SessionStart hook (below) |
   | `list` | The open items, one per line (`#12 [high] Title  (category)`), highest priority first |
   | `export` | Writes the open items, with their text, to `_pending-work/pendingWork.md` |
   | `setup-labels` | Makes or updates the labels (safe to repeat) |
   | `-h`, `--help` | Prints the help and stops |

   The settings at the top of the script, `MIRROR`, `QUEUE` and `CATEGORIES`, may be changed for a project (the
   script is then "changed by hand", and `update` leaves it alone). The folder `_pending-work/` starts with `_`, so
   Quarto does not render it.
3. `.claude/settings.json` runs `pending.sh session-start` for the SessionStart sources `startup` and `clear`, after
   the notice hook (@sec-notice). The output is JSON with:
   - `systemMessage`, which the user sees: the count by priority, for example `Pending work: 12 pending items (3
     high, 5 medium, 4 low). Want to see them? Say "list pending".`, or `Pending work: nothing pending.`;
   - `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, which the agent gets: the same count and how to answer. **It does not
     hold the list**, so that the list uses no context until the user asks for it.
4. When `gh` is missing or not logged in, GitHub cannot be reached, or the project has no GitHub remote,
   `session-start` and `list` use the saved copy (`_pending-work/pendingWork.md`) and the items that the agent
   queued in `_pending-work/queue.md` (headings `### [priority] Title`). The output says that the count may be out
   of date.
5. `SKILL.md` tells the agent how to show, add, change, work on and close items, and how to handle the queue.

## Tests {#sec-tests}

`tests/selftest.py` makes test projects in a scratch folder and checks every function in this SPEC: `new` of each
type (and of v0.2.0), `status` in each state, `update` of existing folders (the plan and its diffs, `--dry-run`,
exit 6 without a terminal, a newer tool file, a file changed by hand, a deleted file, out-of-date shared rules,
`--with-docs`, `--no-pending-work`, `--with-pending-work`, a foreign `docs/_quarto.yml`, a settings file that is not
JSON), the setup notice (its files, the hook command with and without the file, the blocks, the docs page and its
render, the history, the update of a v0.3.0 project, a block without its end line), `setup-computer` with a scratch
`HOME`, the output of `pending.sh session-start` (with no GitHub repository,
so it needs no network), the new-doc script, every error status, and that a Quarto render leaves no uncommitted
change. Every command runs with standard input from `/dev/null`. GitHub Actions runs it and renders this book on each
push. It never runs `--github` without `--dry-run`.
